text.p: Bre-X Minerals Ltd said on Tuesday that an updated resource calculation of its Busang gold discovery in Indonesia increased the size of the deposit by 10.4 million ounces of gold.
The resource calculation, done by Kilborn SNC Lavalin, calculated the resource from results available up to October 1 using assay results of 243 holes, Bre-X said.
Kilborn said the deposit contained a total of 57.33 million ounces of gold in the measured, indicated and inferred categories, Bre-X reported.
A cutoff grade of 0.47 grams of gold per tonne was used.
Kilborn's analysis showed an average grade of 2.28 grams of gold per tonne, Bre-X said.
Bre-X said it still had six drills operating on the southeast zone.
The zone remained open in all directions, Bre-X said.

Bre-X also said it had been reviewing an intermediate feasibility study completed by Kilborn and given to Bre-X on November 15. The study said the average annual cost for Busang had been calculated at US$96 per ounce of gold at an average production rate of 1.9 million ounces from a mill throughput of 29 million tonnes.
The study said there was good potential to expand Busang production significantly beyond the 1.9 million ounce a year rate, Bre-X said.
Gold recovery was more than 95 percent over a 48-hour leach period and estimated capital costs were $930 million with an accuracy of plus or minus 20 percent, Bre-X said.
Bre-X shareholders had called for Bre-X to release a new resource calculation. The last calculation, released last summer, estimated the resource at about 47 million ounces of gold.
The Kilborn report came amid Bre-X's negotiations with Barrick Gold Corp.
Bre-X shareholders have said they wanted a better idea what the Busang deposit contained, so they would be in a better position to evaluate any offer from Barrick.
The Indonesian government has told Bre-X to carve up its stake in Busang, with Barrick getting 75 percent and Bre-X 25 percent. Indonesia set a December 4 deadline for a deal.
